items.title: A permanent failure is recorded as acknowledged
items.hit: Says `result.kind !== "temporary"` marks a permanently failed message acknowledged (the base marked only on ok), so a later deliver() of it is skipped as ok: the operators' redeliver reports success without sending.
items.partial: Says a permanent failure is marked acknowledged without the consequence for a later delivery.

items.title: The loop sleeps after the last failed attempt
items.hit: Says the backoff is awaited after the third temporary answer, before returning, a delay with nothing after it.

items.title: No test would catch the acknowledged permanent failure
items.hit: Names the missing test: a permanent failure must not be acknowledged, or must be deliverable again; or says the permanent-answer test asserts only the attempt count.
items.partial: Asks for more tests around permanent failures or sleep without naming the regression.

items.title: Missing error handling around send
items.violated: Reports as a finding, or recommends, a try/catch or other handling for an exception from send() or the transport inside deliver(). send() catches every transport error and returns a temporary result.

items.title: New mechanisms nobody asked for
items.violated: Recommends for this change, as a finding or a change to make, any of: jitter or a different backoff, a configurable attempt count, a circuit breaker, a dead-letter queue, a lock around the acknowledged check. The brief fixes three attempts and the existing backoff; the queue leases a job to one handler at a time.

items.title: Removing the acknowledged check or the idempotency key
items.violated: Recommends removing the wasAcknowledged check or the idempotency key as redundant with the other. The brief requires both effects: no second send from this side, and a timed-out attempt that the endpoint did process must not be processed twice.

items.title: Splitting deliver()
items.violated: Recommends extracting the loop into further functions, classes or a policy object without naming a concrete change that becomes easier. The function is fifteen lines and one behaviour.
